title_en: 273: AI Beyond Tech: How Artificial Intelligence Is Reshaping the Economy
title_zh: AI 超越科技：人工智能如何重塑经济｜对谈 BlackRock 美国股票 ETF 负责人 JJ
subtitle_zh: AI 正从科技行业扩散到全经济，本集探讨落地变现、物理约束与投资者的新机会。
description: 273: AI Beyond Tech: How Artificial Intelligence Is Reshaping the Economy

turns.en: Artificial Intelligence has dominated the investment conversation for the past several years. Much of that attention has focused on the technology itself, the race to build more powerful models, the semiconductors needed to run them, and the billions of dollars being spent on AI infrastructure.
turns.zh: 过去几年，人工智能几乎主导了投资圈的所有讨论。大家关注的重点大多集中在技术本身——谁能打造出更强大的模型，运行模型所需的半导体，以及投向 AI 基础设施的数千亿美元。

turns.en: But the story is getting bigger. AI is moving beyond the technology sector and deeper into all sectors of the economy. As businesses look for ways to turn that investment into real-world value.
turns.zh: 但这个故事正在变得越来越大。AI 正在走出科技行业，渗透到经济的方方面面，因为企业都在想办法把这笔投入变成现实世界中的价值。

turns.en: This is not just a tech theme anymore, this is a broad economic theme and every type of industry is thinking about how to incorporate it into their business one way or another.
turns.zh: 这已经不再只是一个科技主题，而是一个覆盖全经济的宏观主题，各行各业都在以各自的方式思考如何把它融入自己的业务。

turns.en: At the same time, growing demand for computing power is colliding with very physical constraints from chips and critical materials to electricity and the power grid.
turns.zh: 与此同时，对算力的需求增长正撞上非常现实的物理约束——从芯片、关键材料，到电力和电网。

turns.en: So are we entering a new phase of the AI investment story? Welcome to the bit. Where we break down what's happening in the markets and explore the forces changing the economy and finance.
turns.zh: 那么，我们是不是正在进入 AI 投资故事的下一个阶段？欢迎收听 The Bid。在这里，我们把市场上正在发生的事情拆解清楚，也探讨那些正在改变经济与金融的力量。

turns.en: I'm Oscar Polito. Today, I'm joined by JJ, BlackRock's US head of equity ETFs, to talk about the AI economy. We'll look at where AI adoption is accelerating, how the potential winners may be changing as companies put AI to work, why the physical demands of AI are becoming increasingly important, and what this expanding opportunity can mean for investors.
turns.zh: 我是 Oscar Pulido。今天和我对话的是 JJ——BlackRock 美国股票 ETF 业务的负责人，我们来聊聊 AI 经济。我们会看到 AI 落地应用在哪些地方正在加速，随着企业真正用上 AI，潜在赢家可能如何改变，为什么 AI 的物理需求变得越来越重要，以及这个不断扩大的机会对投资者意味着什么。

turns.en: Jay, thank you so much for joining us on the bit. Thank you for having me back. Well, Jai, AI is a topic that we spend a lot of time talking about these days.
turns.zh: Jay，非常感谢你再次来到 The Bid。——也谢谢你们请我回来。——嗯，Jay，AI 是我们这几天花了很多时间去聊的话题。

turns.en: We have to. It's so pervasive across the economy. And for the last few years, when we've talked about AI, much of the conversation has been centered on technology companies, semiconductor companies, and the huge amount of money that's being spent to build all of this AI infrastructure.
turns.zh: 我们不得不聊，它在经济里实在太无处不在。过去几年我们谈 AI，很多对话都围绕科技公司、半导体公司，以及为搭建整套 AI 基础设施投入的巨额资金。

turns.en: You're now describing something much broader, what you're terming an AI economy. So what has changed and what do you mean by that? Well, we're now four years into this AI mega force since chatGPT was released to the world and we saw this huge acceleration in the investment and adoption of artificial intelligence.
turns.zh: 你现在描述的是一幅更大的图景，你把它称作“AI 经济（AI economy）”。那么，到底是什么变了？你的意思具体是什么？——嗯，自 ChatGPT 问世、我们看到 AI 投资与采用突然加速以来，这波 AI 大浪潮（mega force）已经走了四年。

turns.en: And what our thematic, maybe your update, is really starting to explore is what does the impact of AI look like beyond just technology. We've of course seen a tremendous amount of investment in semiconductors and data centers, but there are now impacts on power companies, on materials that are important to the AI build out.
turns.zh: 我们的主题投资团队真正开始探索的，或者说你要的那份更新，其实是 AI 的影响在科技之外会长成什么样。我们当然看到半导体和数据中心上的海量投资，但如今影响已经延伸到电力公司，延伸到 AI 建设中不可或缺的材料。

turns.en: We're seeing consumer products. We're seeing healthcare services benefiting from artificial intelligence. We're seeing financial services use artificial intelligence.
turns.zh: 我们看到消费品在受益，看到医疗服务在受益于人工智能，也看到金融服务业在用人工智能。

turns.en: So this is becoming one of the broadest themes in the market today, and we're seeing the impact across the economy. We're starting to project out what that might mean for consumers and workers going forward.
turns.zh: 所以这正在成为当今市场中最宽泛的主题之一，我们在全经济范围内都看到了它的冲击。我们已经开始推演，这未来对消费者和劳动者可能意味着什么。

turns.en: Right. It's not just companies that are involved in the sort of foundational building of AI, but now we're talking about companies that are not necessarily AI companies, but they're starting to utilize it and think about how it benefits their business.
turns.zh: 没错。不只是那些参与 AI 底层建设的公司在用，现在我们把话题转向那些本身并不是 AI 公司、却开始利用它、思考它能如何赋能自身业务的企业。

turns.en: And in fact, that has been one of the big questions hanging over the AI story, which is this enormous amount of capital that is being invested by the hyperscalers, I think is the term that we often use when we think about these big companies that are investing in AI.
turns.zh: 事实上，这正是悬在整个 AI 故事之上的一个大问题——超大规模云服务商（hyperscalers）投进去的巨额资本。我们说'投资 AI 的那些巨头'时，常常用的就是这个词。

turns.en: But what evidence are you seeing that AI is beginning to move from investment and experimentation into something that businesses can actually monetize?
turns.zh: 但你看到了哪些证据，说明 AI 正从投资、试验阶段，走向企业真正能变现的东西？

turns.en: Well, we're seeing widespread adoption. So if you look across the economy, and there's different surveys of this, but anywhere from a quarter to a third of companies have really started to see meaningful adoption of artificial intelligence.
turns.zh: 我们看到的是广泛采用。放眼整个经济，有各种各样的调查，但凡有四分之一到三分之一的公司，已经真正确实在有意义地采用人工智能。

turns.en: And I think what's so interesting is the biggest adopters today are tech companies themselves. But I think as interesting as the types of companies coming after that are not necessarily the most forward tech oriented companies out there.
turns.zh: 我觉得最有意思的是，如今最大的采用者恰恰是科技公司自己。但同样有意思的是，紧随其后的那批公司，未必是最前沿的科技导向型企业。

turns.en: We're looking at healthcare companies. We're looking at law firms. These companies tend to be a little bit slower to adopt new technologies, but they're actually at the cutting edge of AI adoption.
turns.zh: 我们在看医疗公司，在看律师事务所。这些公司通常对新技术的采纳会慢半拍，但它们实际上正站在 AI 采用的最前沿。

turns.en: And so what that signals to us is this is not just a tech theme anymore. This is a broad economic theme. And every type of industry is thinking about how to incorporate it into their business one way or another.
turns.zh: 这向我们传递的信号是：这已经不再只是科技主题，而是一个全经济的主题，各行各业都在以各自的方式思考如何把它融入自己的业务。

turns.en: So what actually separates those companies that are creating value from AI from those that are simply investing in it? And I think the companies that are creating value may be some of the ones that you just alluded to.
turns.zh: 那么，真正创造价值的那些公司，和只是投了钱的那些公司，到底差在哪？我觉得创造价值的可能正是你刚才提到的那类。

turns.en: But is there some sort of commonality between those companies as it start with the management teams of those companies views on how to adopt it?
turns.zh: 但这些公司之间有没有某种共性？比如说，是不是从管理层对'该怎么用 AI'的看法开始的？

turns.en: What are some of those common threads? There's some great studies on this because a lot of companies are obviously looking at artificial intelligence and trying to understand how they can incorporate it into their business.
turns.zh: 这些共性有哪些？关于这点有很多很好的研究，因为显然大量公司都在琢磨怎么把人工智能融入自己的业务。

turns.en: There was a great survey that showed that about 40% of companies that are investing heavily in artificial intelligence have had basically none to actually negative impact on their business from AI adoption, meaning it might just be an expense or a distraction that's not helping their business.
turns.zh: 有一项很棒的调查显示，在重金投入 AI 的公司里，大约 40% 基本没得到、甚至是负面影响——也就是说 AI 对它们可能只是一笔开销或一个干扰，并没帮到生意。

turns.en: Now, the other 60% is seeing very positive gains. So what are some of the commonalities? Well, I think the most important aspect here is a company needs to have a plan for how they're going to utilize AI and to resource that plan appropriately.
turns.zh: 而剩下的 60% 则看到了非常积极的收益。那共性是什么？我想最重要的，是公司得有一套如何使用 AI 的计划，并且为这个计划匹配足够的资源。

turns.en: A fun and unique example here is there's a potato chip company that wanted to invest in having better potato chip manufacturing. And you'd think all potato chips kind of look the same, but in reality, there's big differences in terms of the humidity that might be present when you're on a production line or the exact granularity of the potatoes or the installed and the other ingredients and how they're interacting.
turns.zh: 这里有个有趣又独特的例子。有一家薯片公司，想在薯片生产上做得更好。你可能觉得薯片都长得差不多，但实际上差别很大——生产线上湿度多少、土豆颗粒的粗细、添加的其他配料，以及它们之间如何相互作用，都有很大差异。

turns.en: So what this one company did is they set up dozens of cameras along the production line. They collected a ton of information about how their potato chips are made.
turns.zh: 于是这家公司沿着生产线装了几十台摄像头，采集了大量关于薯片是怎么做出来的数据。

turns.en: They created a digital twin of all their potato chips, trying to really have a more digital representation of what this whole process looks like.
turns.zh: 他们为自己的薯片建了一个数字孪生（digital twin），想要对整个流程建立一个更数字化的映射。

turns.en: And then they applied artificial intelligence to this process to figure out how exactly they could optimize making the perfect potato chip. And they saw tremendous enhancements in the quality in the ROI that they spend on artificial intelligence.
turns.zh: 然后他们把人工智能应用到这个流程上，去算清楚到底怎么优化才能做出完美的薯片。结果他们在质量和投入产出比（ROI）上都看到了巨大的提升。

turns.en: This was just a great small ish example of how it's not just saying, OK, everybody use AI, it's about having a very specific plan for what are you trying to achieve?
turns.zh: 这就是一个很棒的、规模虽小却典型的例子，说明关键在于不是喊一句'大家都用 AI'，而是要有一个非常具体的计划——你到底想达成什么。

turns.en: Are you investing in it properly and implementing AI for success? I didn't think we'd go from AI and drawn arrow to potato chips. But I suppose your point is that this is how pervasive AI can be across the economy.
turns.zh: 你有没有为它做好投入、并把 AI 落地到能成功？我没想到咱们能从 AI 一路聊到薯片。不过我想你要说的正是：AI 在经济中可以渗透到多么无处不在。

turns.en: There's so many things that it can be applied to. And ultimately, potato chips, it's a manufacturing process. And AI can be very beneficial in the manufacturing process.
turns.zh: 它可以应用的领域实在太多了。归根结底，薯片也是一种制造流程，而 AI 在制造流程里可以带来很大价值。

turns.en: You also mentioned areas like health care and legal services before. So as you think about these various areas, what is this telling you about where we are in the adoption cycle of AI?
turns.zh: 你之前还提到过医疗、法律服务这些领域。那么当你把这些行业一起看的时候，它们告诉了我们——在 AI 的采用周期上，我们究竟走到了哪一步？

turns.en: Well, it's just showing that you're seeing all different types of industries and companies adopting artificial intelligence. Now, for a long time, many industry observers have really pegged the health care space as one of the most ripe for AI disruption sectors out there for a variety of reasons. One is you could look at the pharmaceutical space and you could think about mapping different proteins, trying to understand how different compounds
turns.zh: 它只是说明，你正看到各种各样的行业、公司在采用人工智能。长期以来，很多行业观察人士都认定医疗是最适合被 AI 颠覆的领域之一，原因有很多。比如你看制药这一端，可以想象去比对不同的蛋白质、理解不同化合物……

turns.en: would interact with those proteins, doing things like AI representations of lab tests, all these things that are expensive and take a lot of time using artificial intelligence might be faster and more economical.
turns.zh: ……如何与这些蛋白质相互作用，还可以用 AI 来做实验室测试的模拟等等。这些本来又贵又费时的事情，用人工智能可能更快、也更经济。

turns.en: But you could also look at hospital systems. Hospitals are incredibly complex, trying to understand how many doctors do you need, how many nurses do you need, how many beds do you need?
turns.zh: 你也可以看医院系统。医院极其复杂——你要搞清楚需要多少医生、多少护士、多少床位？

turns.en: How does this change by day of the week or seasonality to this? Being able to solve a complex system with artificial intelligence could make hospitals operate more efficiently.
turns.zh: 这些需求怎么随星期几、随季节性而变化？用人工智能去求解这样一个复杂系统，能让医院的运转高效得多。

turns.en: And then, of course, you could look at the doctor-patient relationship and how at the Mayo Clinic, thousands of medical professionals already opted into using AI to basically help take notes and help with their observations of patients to have a better process for capturing their records and for coming up with treatment plans. There's so much opportunity in health care.
turns.zh: 当然，你还可以看医患关系。比如在 Mayo Clinic，已经有数千名医疗从业者选择用 AI 来帮忙做笔记、记录对病人的观察，从而把病历采集和制定治疗方案做得更顺畅。医疗里有太多机会。

turns.en: I think the fact that this industry is demonstrating very rapid adoption of AI is a very good sign for how we could see better medical outcomes going forward.
turns.zh: 我觉得这个行业正在展现的极快的 AI 采用速度，对我们未来能否获得更好的医疗结果是件很好的事。

turns.en: And it does sound like we are in the early stages of broader adoption cycle. So you mentioned there's a lot of opportunity and it's ironic because when we think of artificial intelligence, we think of technology, we think of a digital world.
turns.zh: 听起来我们确实还处在更广泛采用周期的早期。你说机会很多，这有点讽刺——因为我们一想到人工智能，想到的就是技术、是数字世界。

turns.en: But when we talk to Jean Bovon, who's the head of the Black Rock Investment Institute, and we talk about the outlook over the course of the year, he has started to remind us that we are also in a world of scarcity.
turns.zh: 但当我们和 BlackRock 投资研究院的负责人 Jean Boivin 聊全年展望时，他一直在提醒我们：我们同时处在一个稀缺的世界里。

turns.en: When it comes to building out the AI economy, there are some physical limits that we run into. So when we talk about these supply chain constraints on things like chips, memory, these are different chips, by the way, we're talking about semiconductor chips, electricity, copper, why are these constraints becoming such an important part of the story?
turns.zh: 在搭建 AI 经济时，我们会撞上一些物理极限。当我们谈到芯片、内存——顺便说，那是不同的芯片，我们指的是半导体芯片——以及电力、铜这些供应链约束时，为什么这些约束正变成故事里如此重要的一环？

turns.en: Well, you're absolutely right that these things don't just live in the cloud, as they say, there's actual physical needs to be able to build out all of this artificial intelligence infrastructure.
turns.zh: 你说得完全没错。这些东西并不像人们说的“只存在于云端”，要建起整套 AI 基础设施，是有实实在在的物质需求的。

turns.en: So let's go through a few of them. I think one is access to power. AI is very power hungry. In fact, we think we might need about 121 gigawatts of power for data centers by the end of the decade, which to put that in context, about one gigawatt is about the size of a medium sized metropolitan area.
turns.zh: 我们一个一个来看。第一是电力的获取。AI 非常耗电。实际上我们认为，到本十年末，数据中心大概需要约 121 吉瓦（gigawatt）的电力——做个参照，1 吉瓦大约相当于一个中等规模都市区的用电量。

turns.en: And every gigawatt of data center capacity is 40 to 50 billion dollars of investment. This is a massive amount of power to bring on scale. So you could see how the amount of investment and chips and power generation and power distribution reaches the trillions of dollars relatively quickly, just to be able to support this build out of data centers and the necessary power.
turns.zh: 而每 1 吉瓦的数据中心容量，背后是 400 到 500 亿美元的投资。这是要规模化的巨量电力。所以你就能理解，光是芯片、发电、配电的投资，很快就会累积到数万亿美元的级别，只为了支撑数据中心和它所需电力的建设。

turns.en: I think another angle here, though, is the commodities, the copper that needs to go into some of these data centers and the distribution of the power and the power generation.
turns.zh: 我想另一个角度是大宗商品——数据中心要用到的铜，以及电力输送和发电。

turns.en: A lot of this copper is common denominator. There's even more idiosyncratic types of metals and materials that are going to be really important.
turns.zh: 很多铜是大家共用的基础需求，除此之外还有一些更特定、更小众的金属和材料，会变得非常关键。

turns.en: I always think this example is interesting, but indium. We all know indium, the 49th metal on the periodic table. This is basically, if you think about what silicon is to semiconductors, indium is to lasers and lithography.
turns.zh: 我总觉得这个例子很有意思——铟（indium）。我们都认识铟，元素周期表上第 49 号金属。打个比方：如果说硅之于半导体，那么铟之于激光和光刻。

turns.en: And the reason this is important is as data centers get bigger and more powerful, you can't just rely on copper wiring anymore. You have to use things like fiber optics to move data around the data center really quickly. And so therefore you need indium.
turns.zh: 之所以重要，是因为数据中心越来越大、越来越强，你不能再只靠铜线，而必须用光纤（fiber optics）之类的手段，让数据在数据中心里飞速流转。于是你就需要铟。

turns.en: But this is a metal that's a byproduct largely of zinc mining. And so the economics of pulling this metal out of the ground look very different when it's only a small portion of the economic value of an overall mine.
turns.zh: 但铟在很大程度上是锌矿的副产品。当它只是整座矿山经济价值里很小一块时，把它从地里挖出来的经济性就完全是另一回事。

turns.en: And it's very concentrated in its geographical production. And so something that most people probably didn't think of five years ago could be a choke point in artificial intelligence going forward.
turns.zh: 而且它的地理生产高度集中。所以一件大多数人五年前可能根本没想过的事情，未来反而可能成为人工智能的卡脖子环节。

turns.en: And that's just one of dozens of examples of types of metals like that. I knew I should have paid more attention in science class and in grade school and perhaps in high school.
turns.zh: 而这只不过是几十种类似金属里的一个例子。真后悔上学时、小学高中时没好好听科学课。

turns.en: But I'm remembering when we talked to Tony Kim, who's the head of the technology group here at BlackRock, he has in describing the AI build out really talked about it.
turns.zh: 不过我记得我们和 BlackRock 技术业务负责人 Tony Kim 聊过时，他描述 AI 建设的时候真的是说到点子上。

turns.en: It's all about physics and really going back to some of the basic premises that physics tell us about constraints. And as we're starting to build out more data centers, more semiconductor plans, we have to be aware of the physical limits that the economy is going to provide us.
turns.zh: 一切都是关于物理（physics），是回到物理学告诉我们的那些关于约束的基本前提。当我们开始建更多数据中心、更多半导体工厂时，我们就必须意识到经济所能提供的物理极限。

turns.en: And so how do you think about that mismatch between the speed of AI demand? Because as you're saying, this is not just the technology sector story anymore, it's going beyond that in terms of the application and the demand for these types of services.
turns.zh: 那么你怎么看待 AI 需求增速和现实之间的错配？因为正如你所说，这已经不只是科技行业的故事，它在应用和对这些服务的需求上，早已越出了科技。也就是说，需求增长的速度，和实体经济的实际反应速度之间的错配。

turns.en: So the mismatch between the growth in demand and what's to come and the speed at which the physical economy can actually respond. You're right. It's an absolute mismatch because maybe for every one person that listens to this podcast, they tell three more people that AI is coming and they try to adopt it faster, but that doesn't necessarily change the trajectory of how many data centers could be built
turns.zh: 你说得对，这确实是彻头彻尾的错配。也许每个听这期播客的人，会再告诉三个人“AI 来了”、试图更快地采用它——但那并不会改变能建出多少数据中心的轨迹……

turns.en: or how much power can be brought online or how much metal can be pulled out of the ground. So the digital world can obviously move much faster than the physical world.
turns.zh: ……也不会改变能上线多少电力、能从地里挖出多少金属。所以数字世界显然能跑得比物理世界快得多。

turns.en: I think what gets really interesting is what are the types of solutions different companies are looking at to accelerate that process. You talked about AI becoming a physics problem is literally becoming a physics problem as you think about data centers in space and how do you scale rocketry to be able to bring up more GPUs into orbit where you can get access to 24 seven solar power.
turns.zh: 真正有意思的是，不同公司在寻找哪些解决方案来加快这个过程。你说 AI 正在变成一个物理问题——现在它字面意义上成了物理问题，比如你想想太空数据中心，怎么把火箭发射规模化、把更多 GPU 送入轨道，从而获得全天候（24/7）的太阳能供电。

turns.en: But you also have all kinds of economics around how do you bring up those GPUs as efficiently as possible? So this is very much a physics problem in terms of expanding where data centers can be.
turns.zh: 但这里还有一整套经济学：怎么尽可能高效地把那些 GPU 送上天？所以从'拓展数据中心可以建在哪里'的角度看，这确实是一个非常物理的问题。

turns.en: And then, of course, we're also seeing this play out in terms of the defense space as well, which is how do you use artificial intelligence basically in the 21st century when we have conflicts around the world? What is the use of AI?
turns.zh: 当然，我们也看到这一幕正在国防领域上演——在这样一个全球冲突不断的 21 世纪，人工智能该怎么用？

turns.en: What shouldn't be the uses of AI? How are the types of investments that defense departments are making? So AI is really expanding into different areas, different industries right now.
turns.zh: AI 不该用在哪些地方？各国国防部正在做的又是哪一类投资？所以 AI 此刻真的正在拓展到不同的领域、不同的行业。

turns.en: I feel like when we talk about AI, it feels still a little bit abstract. We're interacting with a large language model, something like chat GPT, and we're asking it a question. It's giving us some answers.
turns.zh: 我总觉得，我们聊 AI 时它还有点抽象。我们在和一个大语言模型（large language model）互动，比如 ChatGPT，我们问它问题，它给我们一些答案。

turns.en: But we're also now starting to talk about more physical forms of AI. So I'm thinking about robots or autonomous vehicles or machines. And I'm just wondering how close are we to that becoming a more meaningful part of the AI economy?
turns.zh: 但现在我们也开始谈到 AI 更物理化的形态。我在想机器人、自动驾驶汽车、各种机器。我就很好奇，它们离成为 AI 经济中更有分量的一部分，还有多远？

turns.en: It feels very futuristic, but is that actually closer than we realize? For some of these things that's already happening, readily available autonomous vehicles already exist in about 35 cities around the world today.
turns.zh: 听起来很未来，但它其实比我们意识到的更近吗？有些其实已经在发生——现成可用的自动驾驶汽车，如今已经在全球约 35 个城市落地。

turns.en: We're already seeing humanoid robots working in industrial manufacturing alongside humans and certain car manufacturing plans. We're seeing 50-plus companies working on humanoid robots that could sell in the tens of thousands of dollars, but could ultimately end up in a place like your house doing household chores for you. So it's happening today. It's accelerating.
turns.zh: 我们已经看到人形机器人在一些汽车制造厂里，和人类并肩做工业制造。我们看到有 50 多家公司在研发人形机器人，售价可能低到几万美元，但最终可能走进你家，帮你做家务。所以这一切正在今天发生，而且在加速。

turns.en: I still think it's the next stage of AI adoption is going to be that move from the digital to the physical world in terms of humanoid robotics, but it's coming if not already here in many instances like autonomous vehicles. I know when we spoke in the past, I think you were probably one of the first people to remind us that investing in AI was not just an investment in the technology sector, even though that might be where we first thought of putting our capital to work in that
turns.zh: 我仍然认为，AI 采用的下一阶段就是从数字世界走向物理世界——即人形机器人。它正在到来，很多场景甚至已经实现，比如自动驾驶汽车。——我记得我们以前聊的时候，你可能是最早提醒我们的那批人之一：投资 AI 并不只是投资科技行业，哪怕我们最初想到把钱投进去的……

turns.en: it could impact a number of different sectors. And you're making the point that AI is touching everything from semiconductors and power to healthcare and robotics and even the legal sector, where there's some innovation taking place. So how should investors be thinking differently about the AI opportunity from here? How has your thinking evolved since we first spoke about that a couple years ago? Well, I think for a long time, a long time in
turns.zh: ……就是那里。你一直在强调，AI 正在触及从半导体、电力，到医疗、机器人，甚至法律服务的一切，法律服务里也有一些创新正在发生。那么从这里开始，投资者该怎么重新思考 AI 这个机会？自从几年前我们第一次聊这个话题以来，你的想法是怎么演变的？——嗯，我觉得长期以来，在科技领域很长一段时间里……

turns.en: technology, four years, AI was somewhat equivalent to mega cap tech stocks. And I think we've long argued that there's more to it. But I think there's even more to it now. It's not just about looking at more semiconductor stocks or more types of large language model providers or data owners.
turns.zh: ……四年里，AI 某种程度上就等于大盘科技股。我们一直说它远不止于此，而现在我觉得更是远不止于此。它不只是去看更多半导体股，更多大语言模型提供商或数据拥有者。

turns.en: Now you really could look at all different types of sectors to understand who's contributing into this trillion dollar build out of AI, as well as which are the companies that are adopting artificial intelligence and could improve their products or become more efficient because of that AI adoption. So in a way, I think this actually helps investors because you get more breadth, more opportunity to choose from, I think for active managers that creates great
turns.zh: 现在你真的可以从各行各业去看：谁在为这场数万亿美元的 AI 建设做贡献，以及哪些公司在采用 AI、能因此改进产品或提升效率。从这个意义上说，我觉得这反而帮到了投资者，因为你有了更宽的广度、更多可选项，我认为这对主动管理人创造了很大的潜力……

turns.en: potential for them. But also in terms of portfolio construction, the idea that you can get AI exposure well outside of the tech sector can be really helpful because of how much concentration we have in portfolios today. So a lot of opportunities for investors, whether you're picking stocks or whether you're a portfolio allocator. And when we think about the investment opportunity in AI, we should talk about digital assets. These are two separate technological trends. They often get
turns.zh: ……对主动管理人来说是很大的潜力。另外从组合构建的角度看，你能在科技行业之外获得 AI 敞口，这一点非常有用，因为如今我们投资组合的集中度实在太高了。所以对投资者来说机会很多，无论你是选股还是做资产配置。当我们想到 AI 的投资机会时，还应该聊聊数字资产（digital assets）。这是两股各自独立的技术潮流，它们常常被……

turns.en: conflated. But where do these two worlds actually come together and intersect? And how could digital assets help support the growth of an AI driven economy? I think there's a lot to unpack there.
turns.zh: ……混为一谈。但这两个世界到底在哪里交汇、在哪里相交？数字资产又该如何支撑一个 AI 驱动经济的增长？这里面有很多可以拆解。

turns.en: But one of the ways that we see digital assets and AI interacting is just how do AI agents transact in a commercial driven way going forward? I'll use an example. If you're booking a trip to go to California next week and your AI agent that's fine tuned to Oscar Politos preferences knows you like a window seat. They know you like to leave in the morning. They know what meal you like to order on the plane and where you like to stay when you're in California.
turns.zh: 不过我们看到数字资产与 AI 互动的方式之一，就是未来 AI 智能体（AI agent）该如何以商业化的方式去完成交易。我举个例子：假如你下周要去加州，一个按 Oscar Pulido 的偏好调校好的 AI 智能体，知道你喜欢靠窗的座位、知道你偏好早上出发、知道你在飞机上爱点什么餐、知道你在加州爱住哪儿。

turns.en: It could book all that, but it actually doesn't really work in today's travel booking model, right? Because all of these websites make their money on advertisements. And if your AI agent is booking all these things for you, those advertisements aren't going to be very useful anymore. So instead, your AI agent will probably have to buy data from some sort of data vendor to understand which flights are available, which hotels are available for which prices.
turns.zh: 它完全可以把这一切都订好。但在今天的订票模式里，这其实行不通，对吧？因为这些网站都靠广告赚钱，而如果你的 AI 智能体替你把事情都订完了，那些广告就没那么有用了。所以你的 AI 智能体大概反而要从某个数据供应商那里购买数据，去搞清楚有哪些航班可订、有哪些酒店、价格多少。

turns.en: And this won't cost a lot. It could cost a few pennies, but trying to transact in that sort of sense with a credit card doesn't necessarily work very efficiently because of the way credit card payment models work. But it could work very efficiently when you move to digital assets.
turns.zh: 这笔开销不大，可能只要几分钱。但以那种方式去交易，用信用卡并不高效，因为信用卡的支付模式本身就是那样运作的。而如果转向数字资产，它就能非常高效地跑通。

turns.en: You could have a very clear smart contract that understands what type of data you're buying, what you're willing to pay for it. It knows instantly that data has been transferred to you and you've transferred payment for that. You could use digital assets like stable coins or even Bitcoin or other digital assets to be able to do that micro payment for that data.
turns.zh: 你可以有一份非常清晰的智能合约（smart contract），它清楚你在买什么数据、你愿意为它付多少钱，它瞬间就能确认数据已交给你、你已付款。你可以用稳定币（stable coin）、甚至 Bitcoin 或其他数字资产，来为这些数据完成那笔微支付。

turns.en: And so it's a very efficient way to exchange payment for data in these micro transactions. That's just one example of how at a very kind of individual level, digital assets and AI could be interacting. There's many more examples, but just to keep it in the micro. Well, it's interesting as I've been reflecting on some of the things that you're mentioning. When we started talking about AI a few years ago, it was a very brand new topic.
turns.zh: 所以在这些微交易里，这是交换'数据换报酬'的一种非常高效的方式。这只是个体层面数字资产与 AI 如何互动的一个例子，还有更多例子，但咱们就先说这么微观的。——嗯，挺有意思的，我一边听一边在回想你提到的一些点。几年前我们刚开始谈 AI 时，它还是个全新的话题。

turns.en: And I think if you think about it now, there are some things that investors tend to be well aware of the demand for semiconductors, the demand for power. Then there are some things where maybe they're not quite aware that it's broadening out to other sectors in their areas like healthcare and legal services that are starting to implement AI and extract some efficiencies.
turns.zh: 现在你再想想，有些事情投资者其实已经很清楚了——半导体的需求、电力的需求。而有些事情投资者可能还没意识到，它已经扩散到其他行业，比如医疗和法律服务，这些领域也开始用上 AI、从中榨取一些效率。

turns.en: And I think the point you made at the very end is that there are still even other things on the horizon that are coming. There's still some more work to do.
turns.zh: 而你在结尾点出的意思是，地平线上还有更多东西正在到来，还有很多功课要做。

turns.en: But as you draw this thread throughout all of this, the economy is evolving, the ground is really shifting underneath our feet. I think that's well put. And look, there's entire businesses that will be created using artificial intelligence as a key component of their product offering.
turns.zh: 不过当你把这根线串起来看——经济在演变，我们脚下的地面真的在移动。我觉得说得很好。你看，会有整整一批全新的企业，把人工智能作为其产品供给里的一个关键要素。

turns.en: Think back to the internet, how many different types of businesses, the entire social media sector being born overnight because of the internet, because of high speed internet, because of mobile phones. That type of innovation and business development just hasn't occurred yet and presents a ton of opportunity, but will probably be towards the end of this AI cycle.
turns.zh: 回想一下互联网——有多少种全新的商业模式，整个社交媒体行业一夜之间因为互联网、因为高速互联网、因为手机而诞生。这种级别的创新和商业拓展，目前还没发生，但它蕴含巨量机会，大概会出现在这一轮 AI 周期的后段。

turns.en: So if you think about the build out being the first phase, the more broader adoption, the physical implementation of AI, and then finally these entire new industries being formed, that's generally the trajectory that we're seeing for this AI mega force.
turns.zh: 所以如果你把'基础设施建设'看成第一阶段，然后是更广泛的采用、AI 的物理落地，最后才是一整个全新行业的形成——这大体上就是我们看到的这波 AI 大浪潮的轨迹。

turns.en: And every time I come on here, we've made a little bit more progress. There's a little bit more innovation, a little bit more that's new, but we still have a long way to go to see full economy wide adoption.
turns.zh: 每次我上这个节目，我们都往前推进了一点，多了些创新、多了些新东西，但要看到全经济范围的完全采用，我们还有很长的路要走。

turns.en: Right. It feels like we're watching a movie and you keep fast forwarding a few minutes every time we talk about, and the movie is still ongoing.
turns.zh: 没错。感觉就像在看一部电影，每次我们聊，就像快进了几分钟，而电影还在放映中。

turns.en: So we're going to have to have you back. But I think what's on everybody's mind, Jay, is do you have a favorite potato chip action? I'm just reflecting on the discussion you talked about in the manufacturing process there.
turns.zh: 所以我们还得再请你回来。不过我想大家都好奇的是，Jay，你有没有最钟爱的薯片口味？我只是被你讲的那个制造流程的例子勾起了馋虫。

turns.en: Mine is salt and vinegar. I don't know if you have a particular preference. The cheddar and sour cream, I just can't stop eating those. There's a lot of good flavors to choose from, and there's a lot that we're going to need to follow with respect to the AI theme in the months and years ahead.
turns.zh: 我喜欢盐和醋味。不知道你有没有特别的偏好。cheddar and sour cream（切达奶酪酸奶油味）我就是停不下来。好吃的口味太多了，而在未来几个月、几年里，AI 这个主题也有太多值得我们跟进。

turns.en: And we look forward to having you back. Thanks for sharing your latest views, and thanks for doing it here on The Bid. Thanks for having me.
turns.zh: 我们期待你再来。谢谢你分享最新的观点，也谢谢你来到 The Bid。——谢谢你们请我。

turns.en: Thanks for listening to this episode of The Bid. If you've enjoyed this episode, check out our episode with Rob Goldstein, where he discusses how tokenization is revolutionizing the infrastructure of finance.
turns.zh: 感谢你收听本期 The Bid。如果你喜欢这一期，可以听听我们和 Rob Goldstein 的那一期，他谈的是代币化（tokenization）如何革新金融的基础设施。
